texts.preamble: Cc No: 258/1 Smt. Lipika David vs . Sh. Victor David Page No. 1 Of 10 on 7 August, 2015 In The Court Of Ms. Pooja Aggarwal: Metropolitan Magistrate02 : Mahila Court: South District : Saket Courts: New Delhi Cc No: 258/1 Unique Case Id: 02406R073732012 Jurisdiction of Police Station: Safdarjung Enclave In the matter of: Smt. Lipika David W/o Sh. Victor David R/o 249/2, Munirka Village, Opposite Vasant Vihar, New Delhi ......................Aggrieved Versus Sh. Victor David S/o Late Sh. Arul David C/o John (Kerala Store/Vodafone) Dr. Kapoor Wali Gali, Munirka Village, New Delhi Also at: C/o UCool, A244, Near Daya Memorial Hospital Munirka Village, New Delhi ..................Respondent Date of Institution : 30.03.2012. Date of Arguments : 05.08.2015 Date of Judgment : 07.08.2015 Exparte Judgment
texts.facts: 1. By way of the present application filed by Smt. Lipika David (hereinafter referred as ''the aggrieved'') under Section 12 of Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 against her husband Sh. Victor David (hereinafter referred as "the respondent"), CC No: 258/1 Smt. Lipika David Vs. Sh. Victor David Page No. 1 of 10 the aggrieved has sought Protection order under Section 18; Residence Order under Section 19; Monetary Relief under Section 20; Custody of minor child Violet David under Section 21 and compensation/ damages under Section 22 of the Act. 2. Briefly stated, it is the grievance of the aggrieved that after her marriage to the respondent on 20.11.2002 according to Christian Rites and Customs, they started living together as husband and wife but the respondent used to have extra marital relations with other women and when the aggrieved objected for the same, she was abused and beaten up by him. It is also alleged that the respondent works as a A. C. Mechanic and that he had also gone abroad and earned a substantial Cc No: 258/1 Smt. Lipika David vs . Sh. Victor David Page No. 1 Of 10 on 7 August, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28340180/ 1 amount of money but did not give a penny of it to the aggrieved rather he used to sent the money to his elder brother Eric Franklin David. 3. It is further alleged that respondent used to create troubles in the family under the influence liquor and that he also threatened to commit suicide and to put the blame on the aggrieved. It is further alleged that on 03.04.2011 respondent left the house without informing the aggrieved in respect of which the aggrieved lodged a missing complaint with PS Sarojini Nagar and that the respondent was recovered by the police and sent back to the aggrieved. It is also alleged that respondent is in the habit of inflicting injuries on himself. 4. It is alleged that in 2003 aggrieved suffered a miscarriage due to stress and physical abuse by the respondent and when in 2005 the CC No: 258/1 Smt. Lipika David Vs. Sh. Victor David Page No. 2 of 10 aggrieved again conceived, she had to bear all the expenses of medicines and hospitalization with the help of her parents. It is alleged that for ten years the aggrieved has been abused and tortured physically by the respondent, however, the aggrieved after being fed up with the behaviour of the respondent, started living in rented accommodation alongwith her daughter in 2011 as the respondent has deserted her. It is further alleged that Eric Franklin brother of the respondent prevented access of the aggrieved to the flat of her father in law, who is now deceased and who had died intestate, and she claims to have a right in the same. It has been alleged that the respondent abused and tortured the aggrieved without any rhyme and reason and that he also threatened her with dire consequences if she filed any complaint against him in any police station or in court of law. 5. It is alleged that the respondent does not provide money for maintaining the aggrieved or her daughter (who studies in Holy Child Auxillium School) neither looks after her medical needs. It is also alleged that he also does not provide any food, clothes, shelter etc. to the aggrieved, hence the present case. 6. Notice of the applications was issued to respondent who did not appear despite service and appeared on 03.10.2012 only subsequent to issuance of bailable warrants against him by the Ld Predecessor of this court. 7. In his reply as filed on 08.04.2013, the respondent raised preliminary objection that the aggrieved was employed for gain and CC No: 258/1 Smt. Lipika David Vs. Sh. Victor David Page No. 3 of 10 hence could maintain herself. He has not disputed the factum of his marriage with the aggrieved nor has he disputed that he is not residing with the aggrieved since March 2011. He has however attributed the quarrels to instigation and pressure by sister of the aggrieved i.e. Ms Krishna to purchase a house in the name of the aggrieved. The allegations regarding extramarital affairs have been denied as have the allegations regarding miscarriage. Rest of the averments and allegations have been denied on merits. 8. In the rejoinder as filed on 20.05.2013, the aggrieved denied the averments made by the respondent in the reply and reaffirmed the averments made in her application. Cc No: 258/1 Smt. Lipika David vs . Sh. Victor David Page No. 1 Of 10 on 7 August, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28340180/ 2 9. Domestic Incident Report was filed by the Protection officer on 21.08.2013. However as respondent did not join the proceedings despite repeated calls, he was proceeded exparte on 21.08.2013 itself which order was [LEAKAGE_MASK] on 02.01.2014 subject to payment of costs which the respondent did not pay and he was again proceeded exparte on 25.07.2014 by the Ld Predecessor of this court. 10. To prove her case, the aggrieved Lipika David led exparte complainant evidence and examined only herself as CW1 and tendered her evidence by way of affidavit (Ex. CW1/1) and additional affidavit (Ex.CW1/2) on similar lines as her application and also proved the following documents: birth certificate of her daughter Ex.CW1/A; Marriage certificate Ex.CW1/B; One Marriage photograph Ex.CW1/C; Receipt of money order Mark CW1/D, Copy of stitching bill dt. 5.4.2013 Mark CW1/E along with CC No: 258/1 Smt. Lipika David Vs. Sh. Victor David Page No. 4 of 10 original bills of stitching dt. 12.7.2013, 21.10.2014, 18.10.2014 is Ex.CW1/E1. (colly.); Copy of list of stationary items Mark CW1/F, Copy of complaint to the Commissioner of Police dt. 1.8.2014 Ex.CW1/H (colly.), Copy of I card of her husband, Ex.CW1/I. Ex.CW1/G was deexhibited as the aggrieved did not rely on the same.
texts.arguments: However, keeping in view that certain acts of domestic violence have been committed upon the aggrieved in the past which resulted in the present matter, and to further ensure safety and security of the aggrieved, I deem it fit to pass a protection order in favour of the aggrieved whereby the respondent is restrained from communicating, in any manner whatsoever, with the aggrieved and her relatives until further orders. Any default in compliance of this order shall entail a liability Under Section 31 of Protection of Women From Domestic Violence Act 17. Residence Order Under Section 19 of Protection of Women From Domestic Violence Act: The aggrieved has prayed for residence orders to the effect that respondent be ordered to pay the rent of the premises where the aggrieved is residing as per the status of the respondent. 20. As the aggrieved is the wife of the respondent without any means of sustaining herself and her minor daughter, as also keeping in view that it is the legal duty of the respondent being the husband to maintain his minor child, assuming the income of the respondent to be Rs.16,000/ per month, on the scale of balance of convenience, I deem it fit to award a sum of Rs.7,000/ per month to the aggrieved by the respondent as maintenance for herself and her minor child. 22. The default shall be viewed in terms of the judgment of Hon'ble High Court in Gaurav Sondhi Vs. Divya Sondhi-120 DLT(2005)426. 23. Custody Under Section 21 of Protection of Women From Domestic Violence Act:
